title: The Visibility of the Father and the Trinity
english: When the worthy must be revealed. And let Peter write, as it is foretold: the Spirit was sent from heaven; let it be understood in the same way that the Son was sent. For that word is as a word, and this as a saying, and the Spirit sent from God. And because of the knowing that things said from Christ or from the Holy Spirit are also said from the Father through the single will, these are words. For he is neither ignorant nor sent as a slave, nor does he speak or act or come from himself as an opponent.

That no one sees God and Father, except the Son alone and the Holy Spirit; and toward those saying: 'It is not written, then,' he says, 'that the angels see the face of the Father?' Creation does not see God and Father in the way that He is; for this is of a different nature, incorporeal and uncontainable. And toward this is: 'No one shall see my face and live' (Exodus 33:20). But the Scriptures say, at times to see or know the Son alone, and at times the Holy Spirit alone, the God Father, because the Trinity is in a unity of divinity, just as as the Savior says in John: 'Not that anyone has seen the Father, except He who is from God; he has seen the Father' (John 6:46).

And the Son is from God by nature generatively, and the Holy Spirit processionally; and again: 'Nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and whoever the Son shall reveal.' And as when speaking specifically about the Holy Spirit, as Paul writes to the Corinthians, as was foretold, and as Isaiah prophesies: 'Spirit of wisdom and understanding, spirit of knowledge and godliness' (Isa 11:2). It is not written, then, he says, in Matthew from the Savior: 'See, do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you, that their angels in the heavens always see the face of my Father who is in heaven?' (Matt 18:10). Yes; but they see, not as much and as what God is, but according to what they are able to grasp. And the only-begotten and the Holy Spirit...
